# write_blob_to { #labdata.gitutil.write_blob_to }

```python
labdata.gitutil.write_blob_to(repo, blob_sha, dest)
```

Stream the content of a blob to a file.

Git writes straight into `dest`, so peak memory does not grow with the size
of the file.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**repo**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Union](`typing.Union`)\[[Location](`labdata.location.Location`), [Path](`pathlib.Path`), [str](`str`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Working tree holding the blob, on this machine or another.

<code>[**blob_sha**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Blob sha to read.

<code>[**dest**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Path](`pathlib.Path`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   File to write. It is removed again if git fails.

## Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

<code>[:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[GitError](`labdata.gitutil.GitError`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   If git cannot read the blob.
